analysis.title: GS Flow of Funds: Witching Hour (13 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Desk says the technical setup for US equities is changing even as sentiment stays depressed and the macro shows no clear path to resolution. Corporate buybacks, retail inflows and a post-midterm foreign bid are expected to support flows, while mutual fund selling runs into their October year-end.
Concentrated positioning, particularly in the AI trade, is expected to keep rotations under the hood going and require active trading.

Options are pricing historically low daily moves, which the desk reads as low conviction in either direction and mispriced tails. It favors owning optionality in gamma tenors ahead of EPS, the midterms and the Fed.

Buyback blackout exits: the desk estimates about 10% of corporates will be in an open window by the end of this week and 48% by the end of October. November is the second highest month of corporate repurchases on the desk, and the full force of buybacks arrives close to the end of October.

2026 buybacks total about $1.27tn. Information Technology is 46% of the total ($578.6bn, +88% YoY) and Financials is 19% ($237.4bn, -40% YoY). Energy (+480%) and Utilities (+538%) grew the most but together are about 6% of the total.

The GS Sentiment Indicator, which covers institutional, retail and foreign investors, reads -1.3. Readings between -1 and -1.5 have corresponded to an average 1m forward return of +2%. The desk calls positioning a moderate tailwind for US equities.

Foreign investors own 18% of the US equity market versus 2% for hedge funds, and their positioning has been just below the 50th percentile since 2009. Foreign inflows have historically reached about 1.75% of AUM in the six months after midterm elections.

Mutual fund year-end: $2.306tn of active fund assets (678 funds) and $1.736tn of passive fund assets (81 funds) have October year-ends. Tax-motivated selling of this year's laggards tends to abate afterward, and some YTD winners slow, which acts as a contra-momentum dynamic.
October is the 3rd largest month of equity mutual fund and ETF outflows. November and December see consecutive positive inflows, rivaled only by Feb-Mar.

Global equity funds took in +$12bn in the week ending Oct 7, versus +$16bn the prior week. Technology funds had the largest net inflows, then utilities. EM inflows were driven by Brazil funds after the first-round elections, though flows remain low relative to prior election cycles.

Money market funds took in $166.37bn in the week ending Oct 7, versus a 4-week sum of $15.9bn in outflows. The desk says capital remains skittish and unconvicted, with ample cash on the sidelines to deploy if the macro clears, which tends to happen in Nov-Dec.

Breadth: Bloomberg found 13 episodes since 1995 where the 10 largest S&P stocks outperformed equal weight by more than 8% over three months. The median subsequent SPX return was +10.1% over 6 months and +19.6% over 12 months, versus historical medians of +6.9% and +15%.

Hedge funds: gross/net allocation to Info Tech is 21.5%/20.4% of US exposure (87th/83rd percentile over one year, 97th/80th over five years). Tech was the most net bought US sector in 4 of the past 5 weeks but was the most net sold last week (-1.0 SD). HFs bought Industrials at the fastest pace since early January (+1.8 SD) after selling it for 5 straight weeks.

US L/S gross leverage rose 3.8 pts to 213% (53rd percentile one-year). Net leverage rose 0.5 pts to 46.9% (2nd percentile one-year). The US fundamental long/short ratio fell to 1.565 (1st percentile five-year).

CTA positioning in US equities is in the 27th percentile on a 1y lookback and 54th on a 5y lookback despite re-levering. CTAs have sold heavily in Russell stocks and are the shortest in the index since 2023. Tail scenarios in bonds turn CTAs into buyers, and the asymmetry for the S&P 500 is to the downside.

Election vol: since 2000, SPX and NDX vol have seen a quick crush after midterms and then drifted lower into year-end. RUT vol held up relatively better. The NDX-to-SPX vol spread has historically stayed sticky. A lower vol regime could add demand and support a Santa Rally.

sector_views.rationale: Buybacks in the sector are +88% YoY and make up 46% of the total, but HF positioning is crowded and the sector was net sold last week, so rotations in and out of the AI trade are expected.
HFs net bought US Industrials at the fastest pace since early January (+1.8 SD) after selling it for 5 consecutive weeks, driven almost entirely by long buys.

earnings_insights: Q3 earnings season is starting, and the desk expects companies to exit buyback blackout about 1-2 days after reporting. About 10% should be in an open window by the end of the week of 13 Oct and 48% by the end of October.

tension_points.bull_case: Buybacks return as blackouts lift (48% of corporates open by end of October), retail inflows turn positive in Nov-Dec, foreign investors have historically bought about 1.75% of AUM post-midterms, and vol tends to crush after the elections.
tension_points.bear_case: Mutual funds sell into their October year-end, October is the 3rd largest month of equity fund outflows, institutions stay skittish on the macro, and CTA asymmetry for the S&P 500 is to the downside.

tension_points.bull_case: Bloomberg's study of 13 episodes since 1995 shows median SPX returns of +10.1% over 6 months and +19.6% over 12 months after the top 10 stocks beat equal weight by more than 8%.
tension_points.bear_case: Crowded HF positioning in Info Tech (97th percentile of gross allocation on a 5y basis) can sharpen rotations out of the AI trade.
